idea: What does Claude Duet actually change for someone who already works in Claude?
flow: What Duet does on its own: checks your connected apps every few hours, briefs you each morning, drafts the work, and stops for your yes before it sends, pays, signs or deletes.
What people think of Duet: curious and mostly warm, liked for how it looks and for asking first; slow, US-only off a waitlist, and it uses your Claude plan's usage cap.
From asking to approving: it adds few new powers for a power user; it changes who starts the work, and that habit only sticks around a job that comes round every week.
What comes with you and what stays behind: what Claude knows about you and your connected apps come along; files on your laptop don't, and company plans don't have it yet.

Where to hook it in first: one weekly copy-and-paste job whose inputs live in connected apps (client meeting prep, the weekly sales check, chasing unpaid invoices), drafted while you still press send.
ending: No prediction (Krish, 2026-10-26: "lets give weds the same treatment as friday"). His first job for Duet: keeping his notes in Google Drive up to date from his email and calendar, shown before it saves; then the question, which weekly job you paste into Claude only gets done when you remember it; then a word to whoever runs IT.
takeaway: Pick the one weekly Claude job you do by copy and paste; that is your first Duet job.
angle: What the launch page and the can-do reviews don't tell an existing Claude power user: how it changes your behaviour and where to hook it in first.
tone: Observational, witty and positive; reviews named in the article only, the general mood in the videos.
reader: Someone who already runs part of their working week through Claude, on a personal or business account.
agreed: Krish, 2026-10-26: "Your guess is fine, give a real world example that will occur, send them to Teleprompter and then lets get to Friday"
